metaDescription: The whole shop on one page: 63 products pictured with their own prices, the other 155 linked, across eight departments. Every tile says whether you buy it here or via eBay, Amazon or Google Play.

dives.heading: The three pages we would actually send you to
dives.intro: Rather than dumping 218 products on you, here are the three specific places where the value is clearest right now — with the honest reason each one is worth your time.

products.name: WordPress Plugins — One-Time Price
products.summary: Eight self-hosted WordPress plugins from £19, each doing a job that is normally sold as a monthly service — cart recovery, popups, urgency widgets, social proof, chat, search. We wrote them and run them on our own sites.
pros: Replaces a monthly subscription with a single payment
Our own products, so there is no distributor markup
Built so the urgency and social proof features cannot show invented numbers
cons: We wrote them, so this is our own description rather than an independent review
Some need half an hour of configuration to be worth having
products.forWho: WordPress and WooCommerce site owners paying monthly for tools that could be bought once.

products.name: Megastore76 Ministry Suite
products.summary: Five offline ministry tools and all eleven books in one download. It works with no internet connection at all, and everything you type — prayer requests, visit notes — stays on your own computer.
pros: The privacy design is genuine: nothing is uploaded anywhere
A one-off price with no account and no subscription
The eleven books are a real published body of work
cons: £147 is a serious amount and there is no free trial
It does not sync between devices, by design
Future editions are released separately rather than included automatically
products.forWho: Pastors and ministry leaders who want ministry tools that do not send their congregation's confidences to a cloud service.

guide.heading: Four things we would rather tell you ourselves
guide.intro: Every store claims to be trustworthy, so a claim is worth nothing. Here are four specific things that are true about ours, including the one we are currently fixing.

points.h: We have no customer reviews yet
points.p: Not one. There are zero ratings and zero reviews across all 218 products. Every star rating and testimonial you see on this site is therefore absent, because we have not invented any. We would rather show you nothing than show you a number we made up — and in the UK, invented reviews and fake scarcity are a consumer law risk, not just a bad look.

points.h: Most listing pictures are marketing graphics, not photos
points.p: Most listings here carry a seller-made marketing graphic rather than a photograph of the product, and a few of those graphics show a placeholder price that does not match what the store charges. We look at the picture on every page we build, and we leave out any that prints a price, rating, award or review count the store cannot support — and we say so when we do. We never describe a picture as a photograph unless we have checked it. If a listing’s picture looks like a poster rather than a product, trust the price on the page rather than the figure in the image.

points.h: We tell you who you are buying from
points.p: Only 18 of the 218 listings are ours — the WordPress plugins, the source-code tools, the three PDF guides and the Ministry Suite. The other 200 are links out: the button hands you to eBay, Amazon, Google Play or the vendor, and we earn a commission if you buy. Every tile and every listing on this page says which it is, so you find out before you click and not at the checkout. All 218 showed as in stock on 29 September 2026 and 15 were on sale, but stock and prices move, so the listing itself is always the final word.

points.h: The specs you read are the maker's, not ours
points.p: On the tech pages we publish the manufacturer's own figures for noise cancelling, battery life and the rest, and we label them as such. We have not independently tested these products. Where we think a number is optimistic — and 56dB of noise cancelling for under £40 is optimistic — we say so on the page.

points.h: You can ask us before you buy
points.p: There is a phone number and an email address at the bottom of this page and a person at the other end of both. If we think a cheaper listing suits you better, or that nothing in the shop fits what you need, we will tell you that rather than take the click.

points.h: Our own products and everything else are labelled differently
points.p: The WordPress plugins, the source-code tools, the three PDF guides and the Ministry Suite are ours — we wrote them, and you buy them from us on this site. The tech and gadgets are not: 200 of the 218 listings send you to eBay, Amazon, Google Play or the vendor to complete the purchase. Nothing in the shop pretends otherwise — the badge on every tile and the note beside every listing name says where your money goes.

proof.heading: What Megastore76 is
proof.intro: A UK-based store selling tech, its own software and books. Small enough that you can reach the person who runs it.

cards.p: Not a marketplace stall. Real phone number, real email, and a person who answers both.
Nothing in the store is a subscription. You buy it, you own it, there is no renewal to forget about.
18 of the 218 listings are ours. The other 200 are affiliate links out to eBay, Amazon, Google Play or the vendor, and every one of them is labelled as such rather than posing as a product we stock.

proof.slotNote: This is where customer testimonials go on the store's front door. We have none to quote yet, so the space is empty rather than filled with invented ones. Send me real quotes and this becomes the strongest block on the page.

faq.a: Two kinds of listing. Ours, bought on this site: 14 WordPress plugins and source-code tools, three PDF guides, and the £147 Ministry Suite that bundles our tools with the book library — 18 listings in all. Affiliate listings, bought elsewhere: the tech and gadgets (audio, smart devices, smart home, TVs, power banks), ten books by Pastor Mega Philip Mega on Google Play, and a few software reviews — 200 listings, where the button hands you to eBay, Amazon, Google Play or the vendor. 218 in total across eight departments. Every tile on this page is labelled with which it is.

faq.q: Why are there no reviews or star ratings?
faq.a: Because we have none yet — zero across all 218 products. Rather than invent them we leave the space empty. Invented reviews and fabricated scarcity are a consumer law risk in the UK, and they are also the fastest way to lose a customer who finds out.

No. Every product in the store is a one-time purchase. The plugins, the source-code tools, the books and the Ministry Suite are all buy-once. That is deliberate — several of the plugins exist specifically to replace a monthly service you might be paying for.

If you want tech, the audio range is where our prices are strongest — 46 products and a comparison page covering twelve of them. If you run a WordPress site, start with the plugins from £19. If you want books, they start at £3.99. If you are in ministry, look at the £147 Ministry Suite.

Not all of them, and we would rather say so. Most listings carry a seller-made marketing graphic rather than a photograph of the product, and a few of those graphics show a placeholder price that does not match the real one. On the pages we build we look at every picture and leave out any that prints a price, rating, award or review count the store cannot support. So trust the price on the page rather than any figure inside a picture.

faq.q: Can I ask a question before buying?
faq.a: Yes, and we would rather you did. Email megaphilip76@gmail.com or call +44 7869 160958. Tell us what you are trying to do and we will point you at the right listing — or tell you honestly that nothing in the shop fits.
